leading_positions.synthesis: All four propose Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye for optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level, and all four give the same reasons: an original concept (magic-wavelength trapping), independent confirmation with Sr, Yb and Hg, and a two-name credit that maps onto two contributions. They also share the main risk, overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and each says the citation must be drawn narrowly around the lattice concept. They differ on emphasis: Lindroth would also credit Ye's many-body and spin-exchange control, while Olsson would leave that out as a second storyline. Kroll and Pearce say the prize should not rest on the pending SI redefinition of the second. Kroll's Hall-laboratory connection is flagged for the committee to judge. Pearce is the chair and a supporter of this position.

Both propose Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Allan H. MacDonald and Rafi Bistritzer for the magic-angle prediction and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and both value a sharp prediction followed by a surprising experiment that many groups have reproduced. Both also accept the risks: the pairing mechanism is unsettled, about eight years have passed, and first author Yuan Cao is outside the credited names. They differ on fallback: Danielsson names B036 and B012 as alternatives and would not oppose a precision-measurement prize, while Mehlig names B036 and B034 and calls B036 a strong fallback if B022 is judged premature. Mehlig says the citation should state openly that it honours the prediction and the discovery, not every contributor.

Eriksson alone proposes Charles L. Kane, Eugene J. Mele and Laurens W. Molenkamp for the Z2 topological insulator and its HgTe realisation, citing a short, clear chain of prediction and observation. Eriksson himself names the weaknesses: overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize, the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang is deceased), and thin support. Eriksson lists B022 and B036 as alternatives and says B036 would be a serious configuration if the novelty question were answered.

Johansson alone proposes Peter Zoller, Immanuel Bloch and Markus Greiner for optical-lattice quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter, with Zoller as the theory proposal and Bloch and Greiner as the decisive experiments. Johansson acknowledges that this trio excludes Cirac, Esslinger and Jaksch, and that quantum simulation can be called a method rather than a discovery. Johansson moved here from B044 because of closeness to that topic and to the 2025 prize. B022 and B044 are the alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: Every one of the eight explicit configurations is a single prize part: there are four distinct preferred ballots (B036, B022, B054, B046), and no member proposes a two-part prize.

B036 is judged scientifically sound and mature by members across both camps. Even members who prefer other candidates (Danielsson, Mehlig, Eriksson) describe its attribution as the cleanest or name it as a fallback or serious option.

B022 is treated as a high-impact discovery by members on both sides. Even those who prefer B036 (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) call it a strong or striking candidate, and Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce list it as an alternative.
Members agree on the credit risks of B022: Yuan Cao is outside the credited names, and the pairing mechanism is still debated.
Members agree that a B036 citation must be framed around the lattice concept and its 10^-18 realisation, not optical timekeeping in general, to keep it distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.

B017 (Higgs experimental discovery) is no longer in any configuration: its former first-place supporter has moved to B036, and all members who discuss it say attribution between collaborations of thousands and a three-person limit is the obstacle, not the science.
Members who raised B044 (circuit QED) do not put it in a configuration, citing possible overlap with the 2025 prize and the omission of Wallraff.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a distinct discovery or invention or an extension of the frequency-comb (2005) and ion-control (2012) lineages. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce say the magic-wavelength lattice is the distinct step. Danielsson, Mehlig and Eriksson raise the overlap as a real objection; Eriksson says he would take B036 seriously if Kroll and Lindroth showed the magic-wavelength idea is decisive.

Whether a precision-measurement advance (B036, 'another digit' in Olsson's words) should weigh against a new phenomenon opening a field (B022). Danielsson prefers the new phenomenon; Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce prefer measured stability.
Whether topology was already covered by the 2016 prize (B054). Eriksson argues time-reversal-invariant Z2 phases are a different step; Danielsson and Mehlig treat the overlap as a real weakness.

Whether quantum simulation (B046) is a discovery or a method, and whether jamming (B034) is a single sharply defined discovery. Only Mehlig ranked B034 first, and Johansson, Danielsson and Pearce asked what specific result a citation would name.
attribution_disputes: B022: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, is outside the three credited names, and earlier moire band theorists (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and later groups (Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov and others) also have claims. Supporters want the citation to honour the prediction and the discovery only.

B036: Katori (concept and first lattice clocks) and Ye (record accuracy and systematics) are described as two distinct contributions by Kroll and Lindroth, but Lemonde, Gill, Takamoto, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, RIKEN and ion-clock groups have close claims. Kroll and Lindroth do not want to extend the list, and Lindroth and Olsson differ on whether Ye's many-body clock work belongs in the citation.

B054: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that Molenkamp tested and are outside the three names; Zhang's death means it cannot be repaired. Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents work on 3D insulators is a separate allocation.

B046: five credited names for three places. Johansson and Kroll choose Zoller, Bloch and Greiner, but Cirac, Esslinger and Jaksch are excluded, which Johansson calls potentially a decisive injustice. Pearce's opening configuration used Cirac in place of Greiner.

B017: the Higgs credit among Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee and Gianotti is not settled, and two members' opening three-name selections differed (Pearce proposed Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee; Lindroth proposed Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni).
maturity_disputes: B022: Danielsson and Mehlig say replication across many groups and materials makes a 2026 prize defensible. Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce cite the unsettled pairing mechanism, sample-to-sample twist-angle disorder and about eight years since 2018 as reasons to wait. Mehlig argues the prize rests on flat-band-driven correlated phases, not on a theory of superconductivity.

B036: the SI second has not yet been redefined. Kroll cites the pending redefinition as part of the case, while Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce say the discovery stands without it and that the committee should not tie its timing to a metrology decision.
B046: Johansson regards two decades of independent replication as strong maturity but notes the promised payoff for the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram and high-Tc physics has not been delivered.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll: research stay in John Hall's Boulder laboratory as a doctoral student, whose lineage at JILA is linked to Jun Ye's group, so a possible recusal question arises for B036. He reports no documented tie to Katori or Ye and asks the committee to decide.

Olsson: B021 (aberration correction) is her own field of transmission electron microscopy, and she may know its candidates through the microscopy community and IFSM. She would recuse from a final decision on B021 if the ties prove closer than acquaintance. She reports no specific conflict for B036.
Johansson: directs WACQT at Chalmers and works on circuit QED, so he flags a possible recusal issue on B044 and quantum-computing hardware candidates. He reports no conflict for B046, B022 or B036.

Pearce (chair): documented ties to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and a CERN doctoral background, adjacent to B012 and B017. No specific tie to any credited person, and neither is his preferred configuration.

Danielsson (CERN years in the 1990s, string theory) and Eriksson (2025 chair, which bears on B044 overlap) report no specific conflict. Mehlig notes a field affinity for B034 but no personal connection, and Lindroth reports none for B036.
questions_for_round2: B036 versus B022: if the committee must choose between a mature precision-measurement result and a younger field-opening discovery, which criterion governs, and what evidence on the settled interpretation of magic-angle graphene would change the maturity judgement of Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce?

For B036, can supporters draft a one-sentence citation that rests on magic-wavelength lattice trapping and its realisation at 10^-18, state what it leaves to ion clocks and other lattice-clock groups, and say whether Ye's many-body and spin-exchange work is inside it?
For B036, does Kroll's Hall-laboratory connection require recusal, and would the committee's decision be affected if he abstained?

For B022, can Danielsson and Mehlig state how the citation will treat Yuan Cao and the earlier moire-theory contributors within three names, and would they accept B036 if the committee judges that credit gap unrepaired?
For B054, can Eriksson answer the 2016 overlap and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission well enough for members who ranked it sixth or lower to reconsider, or is B054 now an alternative only?
For B046, can Johansson, Kroll and Pearce agree on a defensible three from Zoller, Bloch, Greiner, Cirac and Esslinger, and is quantum simulation a discovery under the prize criterion?
Is any two-part configuration viable inside the three-person limit? Pearce sees no clean pairing with B036, but Danielsson and Mehlig have not stated whether a split involving B022 would work.
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files now name four distinct single-part configurations: B036 (four members), B022 (two), B054 (one) and B046 (one). The two largest groups are separated mainly by how they weigh interpretive maturity against the opening of a new field, and the B036 group's main exposure is novelty relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes. As chair I support B036, so this summary relies only on positions written in the eight files and takes no position beyond them.
